newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's troubled Tyumen Oil Co suspends board.
newsitem.headline: Russia's troubled Tyumen Oil Co suspends board.

text.p: Shareholders of Russia's Tyumen Oil Company (TNK) voted to suspend the company's board of directors and transfer control of the group to shareholders alone, a company spokesman said on Monday.
The vote, which took place at an extraordinary shareholders meeting on Saturday in Moscow, casts further doubts over plans to fully privatise the oil group.
The government was to have offered 48.68 percent of the company in a cash auction on August 5, but said last week it had suspended the auction for an unspecified period and for unspecified reasons.
TNK is one of six energy companies slated for sale to raise much-needed cash for state coffers.

The company's former secretary of the board Sergei Verin told Reuters the State Property Committee, which owns the 48.68 percent, would set a date for another shareholders' meeting and would inform them of the agenda.

The second biggest shareholder in TNK is a unit of the powerful commercial bank Alfa-Group, which won an investment tender for 40 percent of the company last month, bidding $810 million for the shares and investment conditions.
Alfa has said it wants to raise its share of the company to a controlling stake by bidding in the cash auction.
Like several other big privatisations in Russia recently, Alfa's competitors complained that the tender was not won fairly.
It was not clear whether the controversial investment auction was in any way connected with shareholder dissatisfaction or the delay in the cash auction.
